mechanism: Binary counter in swept-token form (filler 2=100; a digit is a token 1 0^k, k>=4, whose bit cell is index k-3) next to a unary marker. Each round does one increment and one marker step. A carry that leaves the left boundary prepends a 3-token, so the left end runs a 4-state prefix cycle (1 3 -> 3 5 -> 3 1 3 -> 3 4 5 -> ... -> 3 2.3 1 3 -> 5 2 5); that is round-level OP/OQ. When the marker reaches the LSB: EAT0 drops a 0-LSB, and EAT1 increments the rest and turns the LSB into a 4-digit walker. The walker soaks up carries and moves one filler left every 2 rounds. Merging into a bit-0 digit (7-digit LSB, then filler plus carry) lets it pass through. Merging into a bit-1 digit leaves a stale '1'. The next carry that reaches a stale '1' starts a multi-bounce cascade (10 -> 00 on the left sweep). The cascade wipes a run of digits to fillers and spawns a new walker: these are the counter resets. Arithmetic only chooses which local case fires. A 4-gram token language has 0 halts under closure fuzzing.
closed_gaps: Counter representation: round start RS(S,P,b,g,m) = 0^inf S P b <E (110)^(g+1) 00 (110)^m 0^inf, with S in swept tokens (digit = token with k>=4 zeros, bit cell at index k-3).
INC0: RS(S,P,0,g+1,m) -> RS(S,P,1,g,m+1) in 8g+16 steps, any LSB prefix (80/80).
EAT0 (LSB bit 0 meets marker): RS(S D 2^h, 1, 0, 0, m) -> RS(S, 1, c, h, m+2) in 3h+14 steps, D a 5-digit with bit c (80/80).
EAT1 (LSB bit 1 meets marker): RS(S 5 2^h, 1, 1, 0, m) -> NM(S (1 3) 2^h, 0, 0, m+2) in 8h+29 steps; marker absorbed, LSB becomes a 4-digit (80/80).
WALK4: RS(S 2^(h+1), 0, 1, g+1, m) -> RS(S 2^h, 0, 0, g+1, m+1); a 4-digit LSB with a carry moves one filler left (60/60).

Generic carry transducer (2 skip; k>=4 set; 2.3 walks left; 3 borrows: (a,j>=2)3 -> (a,j-1)4, '1 3' -> 5, '2.1 3' -> 6) explains the record-level 4/6/7 tokens. On the blank-tape run it predicts every carry it covers exactly.
Coverage from blank to 1e9: 98.88% of 150,891 round transitions predicted exactly, 0 mismatches.
Token alphabet appears finite: 10 interior tokens {1,2,3,4,5,6,7,2.1,2.3,2.5}, LSB prefixes {0,1,2,3,4}, 74 bigrams; no new bigram from 1e9 to 1e10 (671,489 round starts).
Origin of 0^2 inside W: a stale marker created when the B-sweep crosses a lone swept '1' token (10 -> 00).
Halting can only happen via A> 0 1 0 (a dense 1-token) or B reading a 1 that has 1 on its left and 0 on its right.

rounds.result: L4 (806 4-grams) is refuted: exhaustively, words of at most 14 symbols reach 324 halts and 248,016 escapes. The least closed k-gram language over the blank run contains halting words for k = 4, 5, 6, 8 and 10. No CTL certificate: 118 native runs of the extracted busycoq CTL62 decider, none true.

Exhaustive one-round closure of L4, every word of at most 14 symbols: 67,601 words and 1,000,548 concretizations. 752,208 successors stay in L4, 248,016 escape and 324 halt.
The round-2 predictor is exact on all 759,169 covered concretizations (0 mismatches). But 110,054 of these (14.5%) leave L4, so L4 is not closed even under the validated rules.

All 324 halts are unruled CARRY_stop, i.e. a carry meeting a stale 1 (86 words). 285 have a stale 1 right before a bit-1 LSB, in contexts the blank run never shows; 228 of these have a 6-digit '2 3' left of a 3-filler run. The other 39 have two walkers ('4 4') and LSB 2.

Words of at most 10 symbols: 3,546 words, 43,340 concretizations, 9,463 escapes (366 new 4-grams), 9 halts. The smallest is '1 3 2 3 2^3 1 1 <E (110)^2 00 110', which halts at step 197 (card Fig 5). Random long words (20-40 symbols): 4,000 words, 12,034 concretizations, 4,113 escapes, 14 halts.

rounds.result: The structural invariant closes with 0 halts once eats are restricted to normal words. H = LE . pre . X . post holds at most one transient cluster X from a list of 37. Checks: 1,214,968 sampled successors plus an exhaustive small-size pass of 1,983,816 successors. All 670,604 blank-run round starts from 3.2e5 to 1e10 lie inside it, and every closure-stage halting example lies outside it. Missing: a quantitative flush lemma (transients resolve before the marker returns). It holds on the run with slack (max tau/epoch 0.34, 0.10 after 1e9) but is unproved.
closed_gaps: Blank run 3.2e5..1e10: all 771 eat and no-marker events see a normal word (g0: LE D* P1, NM: LE D* P0 b0, LE in {'',3,'3 4','3 2.3'}). EAT0 always gives a normal word, and EAT1 starts a transient epoch.

Flush slack on the run (470 epochs): EAT1 max tau/epoch 0.34 (step 8.1e5), 0.104 after 1e9, median 0.036; EAT0 tau = 0. A transient never has more than 3 normal digits to its right (0/1/2/3 digits: 12,302/6,988/2,976/512 round starts).

Negative results: signature-partitioned 4-grams halt at iteration 4 (21 halts). Shape closure without the flush rule halts at iteration 5 (358 halts), through eats on transient words. So the invariant must forbid eats on transient words.

Epoch check over every normal word with r<=5 digits and gaps 1-3 (37,324 words): INC/CARRY normal 74,648/74,648; EAT0 normal 37,320/37,324 (4 digit-free counters); eat epochs 74,644/74,648 return to normal, 0 halts, max tau 169. With r<=3 and gaps {1,2,4,7}: 4,676/4,680 return, 0 halts.

Shape closure in flush mode from 24 normal shapes: fixed point S444 (recheck 110,388/110,388; r<=3: 297,429/297,429), then S562 with r<=6 and fillers up to 9. Exhaustive pass with r<=2, f 1..4, D* gaps 1..3: 1,983,816 successors, all in S562 except a 5-shape chain that lies inside H. 0 halts and 0 flush violations in every run. All 670,604 run round starts lie in S444.

Hand-written invariant H = LE . pre . X . post (LE 4 forms; pre in {'',D*,d,'D* d'}; X in 37 cluster words; post in {'',D* P1,P1}): 1,024 shapes, 2,182 keys. Closure: 259,323 successors (cap 100), then a verification with 1,214,968/1,214,968 in H (cap 600, fillers 1,2,3,4,7, D* gaps 1,2,4). 0 halts, 0 flush violations.

All 130 stored closure-stage halting examples lie outside H: 70 have >=2 clusters, 58 have one cluster word not on the list ('3 f 1', '3 3 f 1', '4 f P2', ...), and 2 are eats at g=0 on a transient word.
remaining_gaps: Flush lemma (quantitative): at every EAT1 the new marker distance (about the unary U) is at least the flush time tau of the EAT1 output. tau is exponential in the normal digits right of the transient (tau_check: 323 of 8,824 S444 concretizations with 3+ digits right stay transient for 690 rounds), so H must first be refined to post in {P1, (d f){1,3} P1} and that refinement re-closed. Then tau <= c*L and U >= c*L are needed; U/L rises from 2.1 (6.5e5) to about 17 (1e9).
Explicit token-level cascade rules. The shape-level transitions are implicit in S562/H.

rounds.result: Stop rule fires. The bounded-post refinement H_3 (at most 3 normal digits right of the transient) escapes at iteration 1 (867 of 1,054,812 successors have k = 4), and the flush time from NORMAL_EAT words is not linear in L: for LE (1 3 2)^(j+1) 5 2 1 |b1, tau/L rises from 1.2 to 27.3 over j = 0..14 (tau = 2^(j/2+5) - 3 exactly for LE 3, even j). The transient cluster is a slow carry through the run of 1-bits, so the flush bound must be in the counter value (as in #28), not in L. 0 halts in every check.

H_3 is not closed: first escape is the 2.3 walker meeting a bit-1 digit on its left (stale 1 left behind, digit becomes 5, k 3 -> 4); confirmed with tmsim (228 steps). 30 iterations: 1,273,992 successors, k up to 6, still growing. From normal seeds: k up to 8. 0 halts, 0 flush violations.

Run facts: value budget v <= m - 5 at all 647,826 normal round starts, m - v >= 158 at all 245 EAT1s; 1-run above the LSB at EAT1 <= 8; max tau/N 0.351, min m/L 3.4, kmax <= 3.
